item.text: {"text":"Time-aware recommendation models require timestamps aligned to interaction occurrences. TiSASRec models historical pairwise time intervals alongside sequence positions; its implementation accepts temporal inputs explicitly. Item IDs alone cannot identify elapsed time: repeated items and identical truncated histories can correspond to different timestamp sequences. This interface limitation follows from the information available, rather than being resolved by a particular architecture. [TiSASRec paper](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~jmcauley/pdfs/wsdm20b.pdf), [official implementation](https://github.com/JiachengLi1995/TiSASRec).\n\nFor the fixed GRU4Rec interface, the practical implication is to avoid reconstructing timestamps through item-to-time dictionaries or ambiguous sequence lookups. If occurrence-aligned timestamps are available internally, slice and left-pad them together with items; compute historical gaps only from already observed events, and mark the first retained gap unknown unless its predecessor is available. Never use the next target’s timestamp or normalize with future events. Read out the final nonpadding position. When inference provides only item IDs and no unambiguous occurrence identifier, exact historical gaps are unrecoverable; retain an order-based GRU, or use timestamp supervision only during training while keeping inference dependent solely on available inputs. Any missing-time pathway should also be exercised during training. These are engineering deductions from the interface constraints, not experimentally established improvements."}
